life: At first light the faithful bring a cup of milk and a heel of bread, and the priest gives them to whoever is hungry.
light: A lamp burns before it day and night; at dusk the priest relights it from the nearest hearth.
nature: Garlands of whatever is in flower hang on it, and are changed when they wilt.
war: Those going out on the road lay their weapons before it, and take them up again blessed.
knowledge: A name is cut for each child born here, and the names are read aloud at midsummer.
death: The dead are carried past it on their way to the burying ground, and a coin is left for each.
storms: Drovers leave a stone before it when they go up into the hills, and take one away when they come down.
order: Quarrels are settled before it on the first day of the week, and the priest writes down what was agreed.
oceans: Before a boat goes out a cup of its own bilge-water is poured over the stone.

river: It was set up the year {land} took the old bridge, by those who were left on this bank.
The first ferryman set it up, and the fords were counted safe from that day.
pass: It was set up after the winter {land} took a whole drove and the drovers with it.
Whoever comes down off {land} alive stops here first; it was set up for that.
wood: It was set up after the fire in {land}, when the wind turned at the last.
[wood]It was cut from the first tree felled in {land}, to ask pardon of the rest.
lake: It was set up the year {land} rose and did not go down again for a month.
[water]The water of {land} was let into it on the day it was made, and is said never to have gone out.
default: [stone]It is older than {town}: the first settlers found it standing in the {country} and built around it.
{town}'s first priest made it, and their name is cut on the back, worn almost away.
It was set up after the sickness, by those who were left, and the names of the dead are under it.
